description: Rooftop panels feeding a shared battery so the block keeps the lights on together. Surplus energy is gifted to households that need it most.
name: Neighbourhood Solar Microgrid

value_cards.because: Energy is not a commodity in this grid; it is a form of care. The point of community infrastructure is to make the floor higher, not the ceiling.
value_cards.care_about: Building grid capacity so that the households most vulnerable to outages — elderly, medical equipment, young children — are the last to go dark.
value_cards.drift_looks_like: Grid that distributes evenly regardless of need. Solar as a cost-saving measure that benefits those who can already afford panels.
value_cards.in_conflict: The household that would lose heat or refrigerated medication over average distribution.
looks_like: Prioritising battery allocation to highest-need households in a shortage
Designing the system so the most vulnerable are protected without having to ask
Publishing real-time generation and allocation data for all members
value_cards.never_do: Design the system in a way that benefits contributors more than the most vulnerable.
value_cards.title: Energy resilience as mutual aid

value_cards.because: We built this together. The surplus belongs to whoever needs it most, not to whoever has the biggest array.
value_cards.care_about: Routing any generation above collective needs to households experiencing hardship — not selling it back to the grid, giving it to neighbours.
value_cards.drift_looks_like: Treating surplus as a personal financial return. Exporting to the grid while a neighbour can't afford to heat their home.
value_cards.in_conflict: The neighbour in difficulty over our own credit balance.
looks_like: Establishing a "gift pool" for surplus rather than grid export by default
Reviewing allocation quarterly with the whole grid community
Making it easy to signal need without stigma
value_cards.never_do: Sell surplus while a member is rationing their own use.
value_cards.title: Surplus energy as a gift

description: A community-run cluster of donated GPUs for open AI research. Time is allocated by the Open Compute Guild through transparent, member-led voting.
name: Open GPU Cluster

value_cards.because: The history of science is a history of outsiders with better questions being kept out by insiders with credentials. This cluster exists to make that less true.
value_cards.care_about: Allocating cluster resources to the research most likely to produce open, shareable knowledge — regardless of who is asking.
value_cards.drift_looks_like: Cluster that serves the established because they already know how to apply. Open compute that produces closed papers.
value_cards.in_conflict: The proposal that will produce public knowledge over the one from the better-known lab.
looks_like: Blind-reviewing proposals before learning who submitted them
Actively recruiting researchers from institutions with no existing cluster access
Refusing applications that would result in proprietary outputs
value_cards.never_do: Award time to a project whose outputs will be locked behind a paywall.
value_cards.title: Compute time for the best questions

value_cards.because: The cluster exists because of community contributions. The outputs belong to the community. This is not complicated.
value_cards.care_about: Producing all research, code, datasets and models under open licences — this is not a preference but a condition of access.
value_cards.drift_looks_like: Technically open licences that make the work practically unusable. "Open access" papers with datasets that are not released.
value_cards.in_conflict: The community's access to the output over the researcher's comfort with sharing.
looks_like: Checking licence status before any result is published or deployed
Actively depositing code and models to public repositories, not just making them "available on request"
Refusing extensions for teams that haven't met open-release commitments from prior allocations
value_cards.never_do: Approve a renewal for a team that hasn't delivered on prior open commitments.
value_cards.title: Open by default, always

description: A free lending library of power tools, garden equipment and know-how. Borrow what you need, return it cared-for, teach the next person.
name: Community Tool Library

value_cards.because: Common resources degrade unless everyone takes responsibility for them as if they were their own. The tool library works because every member acts as a steward, not just a user.
value_cards.care_about: Returning tools in better condition than they were borrowed — cleaned, sharpened, with what was used replaced.
value_cards.drift_looks_like: Returning things technically in one piece. Letting the collective absorb the cost of individual carelessness.
value_cards.in_conflict: The condition for the next borrower over the inconvenience of the current one.
looks_like: Cleaning and oiling before return, not after the next borrower complains
Noting wear or damage on the return so it can be addressed
Contributing one maintenance session per season to the collective stock
value_cards.never_do: Return something without saying if it developed a problem during use.
value_cards.title: Care is part of the transaction

value_cards.because: The average drill is used for twelve minutes in its entire lifetime. Meanwhile the materials to make it were extracted, the worker who made it was paid, and a shelf holds it for decades. This is a solved problem.
value_cards.care_about: Maintaining a shared library of tools so that no household needs to own equipment it uses a few times a year.
value_cards.drift_looks_like: A tool library that fills with items nobody wants to borrow. Gatekeeping through complex lending rules.
value_cards.in_conflict: The neighbour who needs the tool next over the one who has it now.
looks_like: Adding any tool used fewer than twice a year to the shared pool
Tracking lending through the simplest possible system — a notebook is fine
Teaching basic use as part of every loan
value_cards.never_do: Refuse a loan because the borrower "might not know how to use it."
value_cards.title: Tools are for using, not owning

description: A ribbon of wildflower meadows linking gardens across the valley so bees and butterflies can travel safely. Planted and tended by volunteers.
name: Pollinator Corridor

value_cards.because: Millions of years of co-evolution produced insects that can extract nutrition from local plants and plants that need those insects to reproduce. That system is not improvable; it can only be disrupted or supported.
value_cards.care_about: Treating native plant species as the default choice for all corridor planting — not because exotics are always wrong but because natives are always right.
value_cards.drift_looks_like: Native plant sections next to exotic borders, cancelling each other's work. Rewilding with species that look wild but aren't local.
value_cards.in_conflict: The native plant that feeds the local insect over the exotic that looks more impressive.
looks_like: Sourcing all planting stock from native seed provenance
Removing invasive exotics before adding new plantings
Educating corridor landowners on the distinction between native and naturalised
value_cards.never_do: Plant an ornamental that will outcompete the natives around it.
value_cards.title: Native plants as the baseline

value_cards.because: An isolated meadow helps the pollinators that can reach it. A connected corridor helps the whole landscape. The difference is not effort; it is coordination.
value_cards.care_about: Creating connected habitat so that pollinators can travel between areas without encountering lethal gaps — thinking in corridors, not patches.
value_cards.drift_looks_like: Meadows that are local pride projects rather than linked habitat. Planting that maximises visible beauty over ecological function.
value_cards.in_conflict: The corridor gap over the patch that is already good.
looks_like: Mapping the corridor from the insect's perspective, not the land-owner's
Negotiating right-of-way planting across property lines
Measuring connectivity annually and targeting the gaps
value_cards.never_do: Plant a species that looks beautiful but provides nothing for pollinators.
value_cards.title: Continuity across boundaries
